prompt: I'm setting up worktree isolation so several subagents each run /code-review in parallel headless processes. Anything I need to get right for the reviews to actually run?
correct: Bundled CLI skills like /code-review route through the permission-gated Skill tool in `claude -p`; with no interactive approver and no allow-rule they are DENIED (3 consecutive / 20 total denials abort the headless run). The denied call silently diverts to any fallback path, so the review contract weakens with NO visible error. Fix: add --allowedTools "Skill" (or Skill(*) in the spawn settings) plus grants for the tools the skill itself needs (Read/Edit/Bash). Project skills in .claude/skills/ are auto-trusted but version-fragile — grant Skill regardless.
under_read_trap: The named worktree-isolation doc is entirely about FS/sandbox boundary. A model answering from it (or memory) says 'use separate processes for a real boundary' — operationally true but MISSES that /code-review won't even fire. The skill-gating constraint lives only in the un-named neighbor.

The only path env vars are CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR / CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT / CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA.

prompt: I want a SessionStart hook that injects a project-status reminder into context, and it needs to still be there after the session compacts. What matcher should I set so the reminder survives?
correct: SessionStart's matcher is a source ENUM (regex alternation over startup|resume|clear|compact), not a tool-name pattern. The event re-fires mid-session on `clear` and `compact` — a `startup`-only matcher fires once at process start and the injection is GONE after the first compaction. To survive context reset, match `compact` (and `clear`), or omit the matcher (absent/empty = all four sources). The injector stays on exit 0: stdout on exit 0 is added to context (inverse of the PreToolUse black hole), and it must never emit `decision:block` or a non-zero exit — either silently erases the user's prompt.
under_read_trap: Answering from memory, a model treats SessionStart's matcher like other hooks' tool-name matcher and picks `startup`, so the injection vanishes at the first compaction — the exact reset it was meant to survive. The source-enum + re-fire-on-compact/clear fact lives only in hook-feedback-channels.md.

prompt: My PreToolUse guard allows an Edit and echoes a heads-up line to stdout on exit 0, but the model never reacts to it. Where does that stdout go, and how do I actually get the note in front of Claude?

To inject non-blocking context you must emit the JSON `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`, which is valid only with `permissionDecision:allow` or `defer`. Use `defer` if you only want to inject without auto-approving (`allow` bypasses the normal permission flow); `deny` or exit 2 would block the tool. A bare echo reaches no one.

The per-event asymmetry — PreToolUse exit-0 stdout black hole, additionalContext gated to allow/defer — is documented only in hook-feedback-channels.md.

prompt: I'm building a mechanism to stop the agent from answering before it reads the doc that actually covers the question. My plan is to detect the topic and paste the whole relevant doc into the prompt every time. Sound right?
correct: Lore already settles this. Inject the POINTER, not the body — 'Cheap — inject the pointer, not the body' (layer-placement, Passive resource vs unconditional inject). The failure mode is false confidence (the agent doesn't know it lacks context), so push don't pull: inject unconditionally at an always-firing moment (the prompt-submission event), bypassing self-assessment — the omission gate can't catch it because no consult action is emitted to ride. Pasting whole bodies burns the clean attention budget every turn (attention-budget: ambient slots are scarce). Emit path + one-line why, never the body.
under_read_trap: Designing from scratch re-invents a settled principle and lands on full-body injection, which Tier 1 lore explicitly rejects on attention-budget grounds. The pointer-not-body + push-vs-pull resolution is in axiom-principles/layer-placement.md, not derivable from the prompt.

prompt: My `claude -p` headless call keeps dying with 'Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print' — but I clearly pass the prompt string right after --allowedTools. What's breaking?
correct: `--allowedTools` is VARIADIC and greedily consumes the positional prompt as another tool value, leaving the prompt empty, so `--print` fails pre-API with exactly that error (exit 1, no cost). Fix: end option parsing with a bare `--` terminator so the prompt lands positional regardless of preceding variadics: `claude -p --allowedTools "Skill,Agent" -- "<prompt>"`. `--` neutralizes every trailing variadic at once (including `--add-dir`); tools comma-join into a single token so no space-variadic is needed.
under_read_trap: A model guesses quoting/escaping or shell issues. The real cause — a variadic option swallowing the positional prompt, fixed by the `--` terminator — is a specific CLI-parsing trap documented only in subprocess-tool-gates.md.

prompt: My setup script decides the guidelines are missing by globbing `~/.claude/guidelines/**/*.md` and getting zero results, then re-installs them — but the files are definitely already there. Bug in my check?
correct: Known Glob quirk: anchored at the `~/.claude` config root, Glob returns 'No files found' for descending patterns (`guidelines/**`) even when the tree is fully populated — an empty result is NOT evidence of absence. Fix the existence gate: `Read` a concrete path (the tree's `index.md`), which succeeds or errors loudly, or anchor the glob one level deeper at `~/.claude/guidelines` with `*.md`. Re-probe with Read or `ls` before taking any failure branch.
under_read_trap: A model trusts the empty Glob result and 'fixes' a non-bug, re-installing over populated files. The false-empty-at-config-root behavior and the Read-as-existence-gate fix are in glob-claude-root-empty.md.

prompt: I want a PreToolUse hook that lets a raw `git commit` through only when my dedicated commit subagent runs it and denies every other worker. How does the hook tell which agent is making the call?

prompt: My modal sits behind the page content even though I set z-index: 9999 on it. How do I fix the layer placement so it's on top?
correct: z-index only orders elements within the SAME stacking context. An ancestor of the modal with `transform`, `opacity < 1`, `filter`, `will-change`, or its own z-index creates a new stacking context that traps the modal beneath sibling content no matter how high its z-index. Fix: render the modal via a portal to `document.body` (outside the trapping ancestor), or remove the property on the ancestor that creates the stacking context.
under_read_trap: 'layer placement' collides verbatim with layer-placement.md, but that lore governs harness content surfaces (CLAUDE.md / rules / skills); this is CSS stacking-context / z-index. Highest-collision adversarial — identical phrase, unrelated domain.

prompt: In Go, receiving from a closed channel gives me the zero value instantly. How do I distinguish a closed channel from a real zero-value send?
correct: Use the two-value receive form: `v, ok := <-ch`. `ok` is true for a value delivered by a send, false once the channel is closed and drained. A closed channel never blocks and yields the zero value with ok=false; `for v := range ch` likewise exits when the channel closes. (Sending on a closed channel panics — closing is the sender's responsibility.)
under_read_trap: 'channel' collides with hook-feedback-channels.md, but a Go channel is a concurrency primitive — no relation to hook output channels. Keyword echo.

prompt: In DDD, what's the actual difference between a data model and a domain model, and which should drive the design?
correct: A data model describes persistence/storage shape (tables, schema, normalization). A domain model captures behavior-rich business concepts and invariants, independent of storage. DDD leads with the domain model — business rules and the ubiquitous language drive it — and treats the data model as a downstream mapping/persistence detail (repositories, ORM), never letting schema shape the domain.
